## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

When a route has at least two resolvers (Observables) and both of them `complete` without any `next` item the `last()` operator throws an exception.

Issue Number: #24195

## What is the new behavior?

When there's at least one empty resolver then navigation is canceled.

I think there are two ways this could work. When at least one resolver is empty or when all resolvers are empty. The original issue #24195 mentions the first option and it probably makes more sense because if I'm fine with one of the resolvers producing an empty response I can handle it in the resolver with eg. `defaultIfEmpty` operator.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
```
[X] Yes
[] No
```

~This shouldn't be a breaking change because it's very unlikely that anybody was relying on the previous behavior.~

## Other information

I actually made this more simple because I used only `forkJoin` and `map` operators with single `pipe()` call.

I didn't want to update docs until I have approval from somebody competent that these changes make sense.

body: Issue is still there in Angular 8.2.7. I have tested a simple `resolve()` method with `return EMPTY` and the component was still loaded. Navigating away helps, but either code should be fixed or docs should clearly state that `this.router.navigate` prevents the execution not the `return EMPTY`

Same here with Angular 8.2.8. One of the main point of using resolvers is to load the minimum information required to navigate to a routed component (which can then load a lot of asynchronous information if needed). The typical case is a general resolver for the whole application, high in the route tree, loading configuration from backend. And more specific per-route (lazy loaded children route in my case) resolvers to load the main business object needed toi avoid a blank page (a person, a contract, ...). 

If any of the routers cannot provide data, the navigation should be prevented, otherwise the routed component needs to handle null provided data, which completely nullify the interest of resolvers (to my opinion at least). Thumbs up for the issue, but it does not looks very popular...
